title: Bride of Frankenstein
review: It's wrapped in a cool framing device, and I was generally impressed with the screenwriting, except if it were made today they would have dedicated much more time to the important set pieces. Introducing the bride eight minutes from the end is insane by modern standards. Unimportant but wildly entertaining scenes, like the miniature people and the blind man, last longer than the entire lifespan of the bride. It ends very abruptly and is only 75 minutes. I enjoyed it a lot and would have gone higher with the score if the ending was more fulfilling and there was more of a narrative through line. Instead it was more like an anthology of short stories about the aftermath of Frankenstein. Maybe this is because the idea of a film sequel hadn't been fully solidified yet.
